q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: WITH All_Bars AS (SELECT DISTINCT name FROM bar), Bar_Drinkers AS (SELECT f.bar, COUNT(f.drinker) AS total_num_drinker FROM frequents AS f GROUP BY f.bar), Avg_Bar_Price AS (SELECT s.bar, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price FROM serves AS s GROUP BY s.bar), Most_Freq_Drinker AS (SELECT f.bar, f.drinker AS most_reg_drinker FROM frequents AS f LEFT JOIN (SELECT f1.bar, f1.drinker, f1.times_a_week FROM frequents AS f1 INNER JOIN (SELECT f.bar, MAX(times_a_week) AS most_freq FROM frequents AS f GROUP BY f.bar) AS f2 ON f1.bar = f2.bar AND f1.times_a_week = f2.most_freq) AS maxf ON f.bar = maxf.bar AND f.drinker = maxf.drinker WHERE NOT maxf.drinker IS NULL) SELECT b.name, COALESCE(bd.total_num_drinker, 0) AS total_num_drinker, abp.avg_price, mfd.most_reg_drinker FROM All_Bars AS b LEFT JOIN Bar_Drinkers AS bd ON b.name = bd.bar LEFT JOIN Avg_Bar_Price AS abp ON b.name = abp.bar LEFT JOIN Most_Freq_Drinker AS mfd ON b.name = mfd.bar ORDER BY mfd.most_reg_drinker ASC, bd.total_num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC

Q1 returns a single drinker per bar (lexicographically smallest drinker in case of ties), while Q2 returns all drinkers tied for the maximum times_a_week. This leads to Q2 producing multiple rows per bar when ties exist, whereas Q1 always produces one row per bar.
